title: tune overlaps warning for inheriting classes

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

body:
**Describe the bug**
The new "conflicting relationships" warnings in 1.4 incorrectly flag non-existing conflicts when inheritance (and polymorphic mapping) is used. These warnings clutter application output.

**Expected behavior**
SQLAlchemy should not flag non-conflicting relationships (or provide a mechanism to suppress these warnings). The "overlaps" parameter is too cumbersome when there is a large number of relationships (each possibly with its own backref) are present.

**To Reproduce**
The code below shows a pattern I use frequently in my code. I have a Container object that contains collections of other objects that all derive from the same base class (Element). While the same keys and foreign keys are used for each of the relationships, these relationships will not conflict because they reference different object classes.


```py
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, relationship, backref
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey


engine = create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:', echo=True)
Base = declarative_base()

class Element(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'elements'
    type_class = Column(String)
    __mapper_args__ = {
        'polymorphic_identity':'element',
        'polymorphic_on':type_class
    }

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    container_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('containers.id'))

    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
    
class Box(Element):
    __mapper_args__ = {
        'polymorphic_identity':'box',
    }
    size = Column(Integer)

    def __init__(self, name, size):
        super(Box, self).__init__(name)
        self.size = size

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<Box(name='%s', size='%s')>" % (
            self.name, str(self.size))

class Bag(Element):
    __mapper_args__ = {
        'polymorphic_identity':'bag',
    }
    volume = Column(Integer)

    def __init__(self, name, volume):
        super(Bag, self).__init__(name)
        self.volume = volume

    def __repr__(self):
        return "<Bag(name='%s', volume='%s')>" % (
            self.name, str(self.volume))
    
class Container(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'containers'

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    boxes = relationship("Box", backref="container")
    bags = relationship("Bag", backref="container")
     
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
session = Session()
     
container = Container("Top")
container.boxes = [ Box("big", 10), Box("small", 2) ]
container.bags = [ Bag("sturdy", 5), Bag("flimsy", 3) ]
session.add(container)
session.commit()

for instance in session.query(Container).all():
    print(instance.boxes)
    print(instance.bags)
    

```

**Error**

```
home/lauwers/Workspace/alchemy/env/lib/python3.6/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/relationships.py:3454: SAWarning: relationship 'Bag.container' will copy column containers.id to column elements.container_id, which conflicts with relationship(s): 'Container.boxes' (copies containers.id to elements.container_id). If this is not the intention, consider if these relationships should be linked with back_populates, or if viewonly=True should be applied to one or more if they are read-only. For the less common case that foreign key constraints are partially overlapping, the orm.foreign() annotation can be used to isolate the columns that should be written towards.   The 'overlaps' parameter may be used to remove this warning.
  for (pr, fr_) in other_props
/home/lauwers/Workspace/alchemy/env/lib/python3.6/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/relationships.py:3454: SAWarning: relationship 'Container.bags' will copy column containers.id to column elements.container_id, which conflicts with relationship(s): 'Box.container' (copies containers.id to elements.container_id). If this is not the intention, consider if these relationships should be linked with back_populates, or if viewonly=True should be applied to one or more if they are read-only. For the less common case that foreign key constraints are partially overlapping, the orm.foreign() annotation can be used to isolate the columns that should be written towards.   The 'overlaps' parameter may be used to remove this warning.
  for (pr, fr_) in other_props

```

**Versions.**
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04LTS
 - Python: 3.6
 - SQLAlchemy: 1.4.4
 - Database:
